summary: The note argues that SMEs must adapt to shifts in local consumer behavior in late 2023, as Millennials and Gen Z prioritize sustainability, personalization and convenience. It gives examples of local businesses adapting through e-commerce, microinfluencer marketing, sustainable packaging, local authenticity, virtual services, hyper-local marketing and technology. It concludes that SMEs and local communities have a symbiotic relationship.
one_line: SMEs are thriving in late 2023 by adapting to local consumer shifts through e-commerce, sustainability, influencer marketing, hyper-local campaigns and technology.
key_facts: A TrendScope study released October 15th found younger consumers (Millennials and Gen Z) prioritize sustainability, personalized experiences, and convenience.
John Dough, CEO of Dough Innovations, said on November 2nd that the company revamped product lines with eco-friendly materials and invested in AI-based customer service.
An eMarket Solutions survey in December 2023 showed 80% of local consumers prefer shopping online at least part of the time.
Emily Stone of boutique Wares of the City took her business online in late September after a downturn in foot traffic.
On October 21st, Green Bites partnered with fitness influencer Max Health, resulting in a 30% increase in online orders.
MiniPack Solutions, a local packaging company, introduced biodegradable packaging on October 10th and reported significant interest from other local businesses.
Craft Beer Co., founded by Greg Harrison, launched the 'Hometown Heroes' beer series on September 15th with flavors inspired by local landmarks and history, boosting sales and brand loyalty.
Book a Buddy, founded by Lisa Frank, added virtual consultations in late September and saw a 40% increase in service inquiries.
Patel's Groceries, owned by Ravi Patel, started a hyper-local marketing campaign on September 20th to build a loyal community customer base.
TechHome Electronics introduced a smart inventory system on December 1st.
Collaborating with microinfluencers works because local consumers trust peers and relatable figures.
